transmitter_id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: The remote transmitter to set the pin value on. Defaults to the first one defined in the configuration.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

value.docs:
**bool**: The output value of the pin.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

digital_write.docs: This [action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions) sets the output value of the pin.

data.docs:
**0-7 bytes list**: The code to send. Usually you only need to copy this directly from the dumper output. Defaults to `[]`

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

destination_address.docs:
**int**: The destination address to send the command to, see received messages for more info.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

message_id.docs:
**int**: The message ID, see dumper output for more info. Defaults to a randomly generated ID if this message is not a reply or retransmission.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

message_type.docs:
**int**: The message type, see dumper output for more info. The highest bit indicates a reply.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

retransmission.docs:
**boolean**: Should only be `true` if this message has been transmitted before with the same `message_id`. Typically, messages are transmitted up to three times with a 1 second interval if no reply is received. Defaults to `false`.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

source_address.docs:
**int**: The source address to send the command from, see received messages for more info. For indoor stations the last byte of the address represents the apartment number set by the dials on the back of the indoor station and is transmitted in hexadecimal format.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

three_byte_address.docs:
**boolean**: The length of the source and destination address. `false` means two bytes and `true` means three bytes. Please check the received messages to see which address length is used by your system. For example, `[XXXX > XXXX]` appears in the receiver log for two byte addresses and `[XXXXXX > XXXXXX]` for three byte addresses. Defaults to `false`.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

transmit_abbwelcome.docs: This [action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions) sends a ABB-Welcome message to the intercom bus. The message type, addresses, address length and data can vary a lot between ABB-Welcome systems. Please refer to the received messages while performing actions like ringing a doorbell or opening a door.

Use `command_repeats` to control how many identical frames are sent; defaults to 2.

eot_level.docs:
**boolean**: Overrides the default end of transmit level. Defaults to `false` unless `pin` is set to inverted or open-drain.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: Manually specify the ID used for code generation. Useful when multiple transmitters are connected to a single device.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

non_blocking.docs:
**boolean**: If enabled, any transmit will return immediately and the RMT will run in the background. The `on_complete` automation will trigger after the transmit completes. Defaults to `true`.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

on_complete.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations)**: An automation to perform after data has been sent. Useful if the radio / IR hardware needs to change state or power off.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

on_transmit.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations)**: An automation to perform before data is sent. Useful if the radio / IR hardware needs to change state or power on.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

pin.docs:
**[Pin](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#pin)**: The pin to transmit the remote signal on.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

rmt_symbols.docs:
**int**: When `use_dma` is enabled, this sets the size of the driver's internal DMA buffer. When DMA is disabled, it specifies how much RMT memory is allocated to the component. RMT memory is shared across all components and should be allocated in multiples of the block size. On the `ESP32` and `ESP32-S2` variants, RMT memory is shared between RX and TX components. On other variants, RX and TX have dedicated RMT memory.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*

use_dma.docs:
**boolean**: Enable DMA on variants that support it. If enabled `rmt_symbols` controls the DMA buffer size and can be set to a large value.

*See also: [Remote Transmitter](https://esphome.io/components/remote_transmitter#configuration-variables)*
